column1: # SHARD BAR REGISTRY — the ONLY bar source tools/auto_gate.py will act on.
# ⛔ WHY THIS FILE EXISTS RATHER THAN A COLUMN IN THE WORKLIST.
# The obvious place is a 6th column in scratchpad/corefill_work.txt. It is not
# safe: corefill.sh:142 and worker.sh's G4 both read the row with
# `read -r SH TR CT TG SL`, so a 6th field lands INSIDE $SL. corefill.sh then
# passes $SL unquoted to overnight.sh (:169) and worker.sh's G4 refuses a
# non-numeric seedbase outright. A bar column would corrupt the seed partition
# on the local runner and be REFUSED on every remote worker.
# `orchestrate.sh gen` also strips comments, so a `# BAR ...` comment line in
# the worklist would never reach a remote host either.
# ⇒ ONE registry, read by the gate only, invisible to every runner.
# ⛔ AND WHY IT IS NOT DERIVED FROM docs/prereg/ BY GREP.
# Preregs do NOT key their bar to a shard id. Five separate preregs contain the
# beltsever) and they carry THREE different bars (51.93 / 53.32). "The prereg
# that names the shard" is not a function — it is a one-to-many relation, and
# an auto-picker resolving it would eventually cite a cross-reference as a
# registration. A human writes the row and cites the line. That citation is the
# thing that makes the stop defensible.
#   shard      the shard id as it appears in the worklist / TSV
#   direction  ge = the arm must reach >= bar (normal screen)
#              le = the arm must fall  <= bar (ABLATION: low means the flag helps)
#   source     file:line of the locked prereg the number was read from
# ⛔⛔ DIRECTION `le` DISABLES AUTO-STOP ENTIRELY FOR THAT SHARD, INCLUDING THE
# CATASTROPHE RULE. An ablation arm at 30% is its hypothesis SUCCEEDING, not a
# catastrophe; the pinned catastrophe clause (CI upper < 45) was written for
# `ge` arms and would kill an inverted arm at the moment it proved its point.
# Registering an ablation arm here is what protects it. An UNREGISTERED
# ablation arm is indistinguishable from an unregistered normal arm and IS
# exposed to the catastrophe rule — register ablations before they reach n=400.
